content.comment_body: Hi, I'm new to working with [product_name] and am encountering difficulties with Ethernet communication. I am trying to retrieve a program from a client's [product_name] using my laptop, which lacks a native Ethernet port, so I'm accessing it via a Lenovo USB docking station. When I use [product_name] software and go to Tools -> Transfer, all options are unavailable. I suspect the issue may be due to IP addresses, but I can't change my client's [product_name] IP address, and changing my PC's network address hasn't helped. Pinging the [product_name] fails every time. Does anyone have suggestions to resolve this?

Hello, If your laptop doesn’t have Ethernet or WiFi connectivity, then establishing communication through Ethernet is not possible. Both your device and the [product_name] need to be on the same network. Since you can’t ping the [product_name], there may be a network or IP configuration issue on either your laptop or the [product_name]. If the transfer options are all inactive, perhaps your PC doesn’t have a network available, or you’re using a demo version of the [product_name] software. Can you provide more details about your device configuration? Greetings, [user_name] (translated with Google)

Good morning, thank you for your response. I do have Ethernet connectivity using the Lenovo docking station ([url]). Not sure if this is affecting the connection to the [product_name]. After updating the software version from the trial to [version_no], the issue with the inactive transfer menu disappeared. However, testing the connection with [product_name] now says 'unable to access the remote device.' The [product_name]'s IP address is 192.168.1.171, with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. I set my laptop’s TCP/IPv4 settings to a similar IP: 192.168.1.170, with the same subnet mask, and left DNS servers blank since I’m unsure what to enter. I’ve attached a screenshot of my network configuration. (I’m not sure why the message distorts the layout each time.)

You've enabled IPv6 in your settings, and it might be taking priority. Try disabling IPv6. DNS is primarily for internet address resolution and isn't needed for connecting to the [product_name]. If you have a licensed [product_name] [version_no], your available network adapters should appear in the transfer window—make sure to select 'Lenovo USB Ethernet' in your case.
I tried your recommendations this morning, but it still didn’t work at first. However, when I disconnected WiFi, it finally communicated as expected! Thank you very much for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing Ethernet connectivity challenges when trying to interact with the [product_name] using laptops lacking integrated Ethernet ports and relying on external adapters. Initial issues included inactive transfer features due to running a trial software version and incorrect network configurations. Users experienced confusion over network adapter selection and how simultaneous WiFi and Ethernet connections affected communication.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects straightforward Ethernet connectivity between their laptop and [product_name], even when using external network hardware. They seek clear instructions and effective troubleshooting guidance for optimal network setup.
